newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells 319,300 shares at 127 LE each.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells 319,300 shares at 127 LE each.

text.p: The Egyptian state Bank of Alexandria share offering of 1.2 million shares in Egyptian American Bank (EAB) was oversubscribed, one of the agents for the sale said on Sunday.
"EAB was, in terms of demand, covered more than two times fully at the price of 110 to 112 pounds, which seems like an acceptable market P/E," said Neveen al-Tahry of EAB Delta.
"However Bank of Alexandria stuck to their original price," al-Tahry said. "They (the remaining shares) are being kept by Bank of Alexandria."
The Capital Markets Authority said that 319,300 shares were sold at 127 pounds per share, raising 40.5 million pounds.
The 1.2 million shares offered represent 10 percent of the total equity of EAB, which began as a joint venture between Bank of Alexandria and Amex Holdings of the United States.
The state bank's majority holding was diluted to 42.5 percent last year when EAB issued two million new shares, taking the total to 12 million.
It sold 1.5 million shares at 60.00 pounds a share through the stock exchange and offered the remaining 500,000 shares to company employees.
EAB closed down 6.35 pounds at 120.65 pounds on Sunday.
Egyptian American Bank made net profits of 22.9 million pounds in the first quarter of 1997, against 90.6 million for the whole of 1996.
